classes.blurb: MotoAmerica’s premier race class, Superbike showcases America’s and some of the world’s best motorcycle road racers aboard high-horsepower, highly modified, production-based liter-class motorcycles that are capable of speeds approaching 200 miles per hour. These machines are positively bristling with the latest engine, electronics, chassis and suspension, and tire technologies.
classes.engine_configurations:
Over 750cc up to 1000cc, 4-stroke, 3- and 4-cylinder
Over 850cc up to 1200cc, 4-stroke, 2-cylinder
210+ Horsepower

classes.blurb: MotoAmerica’s middleweight championship, the Supersport class features the series’ rising stars competing aboard production-based motorcycles that are slightly less powerful than Superbikes, but are no less exciting to watch.
classes.engine_configurations:
Over 400cc up to 636cc, 4-stroke, 4-cylinder
Over 500cc up to 890cc, 4-stroke, 3-cylinder
Over 600cc up to 955cc, 4-stroke, 2-cylinder
130 Horsepower

classes.blurb: Putting lighter-weight, twin-cylinder motorcycles in the spotlight, the MotoAmerica Twins Cup Championship is a rapidly evolving race class that initially enabled regional and club racers from around the country to step up to the MotoAmerica series and compete on a national level.
The MotoAmerica Talent Cup Championship assists America’s young road racers in reaching the highest level of the sport.

What started as a novel idea has become one of MotoAmerica’s most popular and fastest-growing race classes. Touring motorcycles from Harley-Davidson and Indian form the basis for the Mission King Of The Baggers Championship, but these motorcycles are far from gentle cruisers.

The Mission Super Hooligan National Championship (MSHNC) was created by Roland Sands Design in conjunction with MotoAmerica, and it features motorcycles from various disciplines, along with a broad set of rules meant to bring new riders and brands into road racing.
